content:
iPadOS and macOS used to be very different software platforms, but since the launch of iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year the trend is even more pronounced — iPadOS 27 adds three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac than ever before.

#1: Status Bar Shows App Name

I personally use an M5 iPad Pro that has a Magic Keyboard attached most of the time. For keyboard users, the iPad has long had an issue: there's no clear indicator of which app is currently in use.

If you only have one app on screen, that's not a problem. But when multiple apps are visible at the same time, keyboard shortcuts become very difficult to use. I can't count how many times I've expected a shortcut to trigger in one app, only to discover it actually ran in a different app.

The Mac solved this problem long ago, displaying the name of the active app in the top-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 has followed suit.

iPadOS 27 users will see the name of the active app in the status bar, next to information such as the time and date. Although this is a small change, it's a very welcome one, making the experience of using an iPad with a keyboard much more pleasant.

#2: Permanently Visible Menu Bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the ability to set the menu bar to remain visible at all times.

Last year Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time. However, unlike on the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, a new toggle has been added under the "Multitasking & Gestures" section in Settings, called "Auto-show and hide menu bar".

Once you turn this option off, the menu bar remains visible at all times. I've been using this setting throughout the iPadOS beta period, and it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday Operations Feel More Like a Mac

Although I love my iPad and I'm very grateful for the new features in iPadOS 26 and 27, there are times when the speed of some basic operations can be frustrating. Earlier this year, for example, I wrote: "Right-clicking in iPadOS often feels slow and laggy, but on the Mac it's instantaneous."

Thanks to Apple's greater focus on bug fixes this year, I'm happy to report that iPadOS 27 has improved the speed of these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says that when using a mouse, right-click menus now open faster — and I can definitely feel the difference. Browsing files and transferring them to an external drive is now "up to 5 times faster", and Apple says this is now as fast as Finder on the Mac. App launching is more responsive, and window management is also faster when closing, switching, or dragging windows.

There are still some areas where the Mac is faster and the iPad can feel a little sluggish. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a significant step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Feel free to share them with us in the comments section.
